mcqs.prompt: Red must ferments with black-grape skins. Which contribution comes particularly from those skins?

options.text: Dissolved carbon dioxide and spirit
Tartrate crystals and added yeast
Bottle-ageing sediment and cork aroma
Colour and tannin

mcqs.explanation: Skin contact supplies red colour and can extract tannin and flavour; black-grape flesh alone usually does not explain a red wine colour.

mcqs.prompt: Successful flowering and fertilisation have just occurred. What event produces the young berries?

options.text: Veraison before flowering
Fruit set
Winter dormancy
Bottling

mcqs.explanation: After flowering and successful fertilisation, flowers can develop into young grape berries: fruit set.

mcqs.prompt: During normal berry ripening after veraison, what broad change is expected?

options.text: Sugar tends to rise while acidity declines
Sugar tends to fall while acidity rises
Both sugar and acidity remain fixed
Alcohol accumulates in the intact berry instead of sugar

mcqs.explanation: As berries ripen after veraison, sugars generally increase and acids decline; cultivar, weather and intended wine style affect harvest timing.

mcqs.prompt: Which order describes the main stages before grapes become wine?

options.text: Harvest, flowering, berry ripening
Berry ripening, flowering, harvest
Flowering, harvest, berry formation
Flowering, berry ripening, harvest

mcqs.explanation: Flowering precedes berry formation and ripening; harvest follows when the fruit reaches the composition wanted for the wine.

mcqs.prompt: Other factors being comparable, a cooler growing site commonly helps fruit retain which component?

options.text: New-oak tannin
Fermentation carbon dioxide
Acidity
Added grape spirit

mcqs.explanation: Cooler conditions commonly slow ripening and retain acidity. Warm-region wines can remain fresh where altitude, cool nights or other cooling influences help.

mcqs.prompt: Why should a grower match a grape variety to the site’s growing season?

options.text: Every variety ripens in the same number of days
It needs suitable warmth and light to reach the intended maturity
The variety name fixes alcohol before ripening
Sunlight replaces the vine’s water supply

mcqs.explanation: Light supports photosynthesis and heat influences growth and ripening; a variety must reach suitable maturity within its local growing season.

mcqs.prompt: When yeast ferments grape sugars, what are the main products?

options.text: Alcohol and carbon dioxide
Tannin and oxygen
Malic acid and grape skins
Water and oak extract alone

mcqs.explanation: Yeast transforms fermentable grape sugars into ethyl alcohol and carbon dioxide during alcoholic fermentation.

mcqs.prompt: A fermentation ends before all grape sugar is consumed. What may the remaining sugar contribute?

options.text: Red colour from white pulp
Tannin supplied by yeast
Guaranteed bottle stability
Sweetness

mcqs.explanation: Sweetness can remain when fermentation does not consume all available sugars; the amount left and the wine acidity affect perceived sweetness.

mcqs.prompt: In the common production sequence for a white wine without deliberate skin contact, when is the juice pressed away from the skins?

options.text: After spirit has been added during fermentation
After disgorgement
Before alcoholic fermentation
Only after bottle ageing

mcqs.explanation: For most white wine, pressing separates juice from skins before the juice ferments. Deliberate skin-contact white styles are an exception.

mcqs.prompt: Which step distinguishes the common red-wine fermentation sequence?

options.text: Fermenting the cork with clear juice
Fermenting the liquid in contact with black-grape skins
Removing all skins before any fermentation begins
Adding carbon dioxide directly to obtain red colour

mcqs.explanation: Most red wine ferments in contact with black-grape skins, extracting colour and tannin, before the liquid is separated from the solids.

mcqs.prompt: A producer wants a pale pink rosé from black grapes. Which approach directly limits colour extraction?

options.text: Brief skin contact followed by separating the pink juice
Prolonged skin fermentation and intensive extraction
Adding a high dose of yeast after bottling
Freezing the bottle after fermentation

mcqs.explanation: Brief contact with black-grape skins extracts a smaller amount of colour; the pink juice is separated and normally fermented without those skins.

mcqs.prompt: Which set describes important components supplied by grape pulp?

options.text: Only pigment and tannin
Yeast lees, oak lactones and cork
Grape spirit, tirage sugar and dosage
Water, sugars, acids and aroma compounds

mcqs.explanation: Grape pulp contains water, sugars, acids and aroma compounds; sugar and acid levels help growers judge ripeness for a chosen wine style.

mcqs.prompt: Which description identifies a still wine?

options.text: A wine made without alcoholic fermentation
Any wine to which grape spirit has been added
A wine without the pronounced bubbles of sparkling wine
A wine that must be dry and white

mcqs.explanation: Still wine does not have the pronounced bubbles that characterise sparkling wine. Still wines can be white, rosé or red.

mcqs.prompt: What escapes as bubbles when sparkling wine is opened and poured?

options.text: Oxygen produced by cork
Dissolved carbon dioxide
Dissolved tannin
Liquid grape sugar

mcqs.explanation: Sparkling wine releases dissolved carbon dioxide as bubbles when opened and poured; colour or sweetness alone does not define this wine type.

mcqs.prompt: What production feature distinguishes a fortified wine?

options.text: Addition of spirit or alcohol of grape origin
Bottle colour must be brown
All fermentation must take place in bottle
All examples must be dry

mcqs.explanation: Fortified wines receive added spirit or alcohol of grape origin. Their sweetness varies with the production method and style.

mcqs.prompt: A dry wine smells intensely of ripe fruit. What does dry describe here?

options.text: Absence of fruit aromas
Low acidity
Absence of alcoholic fermentation
Little or no perceived sweetness

mcqs.explanation: Dry describes little or no perceived sweetness. Ripe fruit aromas alone do not establish that a wine contains noticeable residual sugar.

mcqs.prompt: A sip produces a sour, mouth-watering sensation. Which component is being assessed?

options.text: Oak aroma
Residual yeast sediment
Acidity
Tannin

mcqs.explanation: Acidity tastes sour and encourages salivation; compare the mouth-watering sensation with the wine sweetness rather than judging acidity from aroma alone.

mcqs.prompt: A red wine leaves a drying, gripping sensation on the gums. Which term describes this component?

options.text: Carbon dioxide
Tannin
Acidity
Sweetness

mcqs.explanation: Tannin can create a drying, gripping or astringent mouth sensation. This differs from the salivation caused by acidity.

mcqs.prompt: Which sensation can be associated with a higher alcohol level?

options.text: Warming in the mouth
Salivation alone
A green colour at the rim
A coating of visible crystals

mcqs.explanation: Alcohol can give a warming sensation and contribute to wine body; the sensation varies with alcohol level and the balance of other components.

mcqs.prompt: In a wine description, what does full body refer to?

options.text: A fully filled bottle
A legally required sugar level
The size of the vineyard
Greater perceived weight or fullness in the mouth

mcqs.explanation: Body is the impression of weight or fullness in the mouth, described from light to full; several components contribute to that impression.

mcqs.prompt: A grape wine is described as having apple and citrus aromas. What is the sensible interpretation?

options.text: The wine must be sweet
The wine cannot contain grape-derived aromas
These describe sensory impressions rather than proving added fruit
The producer must have fermented apple juice

mcqs.explanation: Apple, citrus, berry and other fruit terms describe aroma or flavour impressions; they do not imply that those fruits were added to grape wine.

mcqs.prompt: Which aroma set can arise through oak contact?

options.text: Dissolved carbon dioxide alone
Vanilla, toast and sweet spice
Only fresh citrus and green apple
Salt, sugar and acid as aroma compounds

mcqs.explanation: Oak maturation can contribute vanilla, toast or sweet spice aromas; their presence and strength depend on the wood and the way it is used.

mcqs.prompt: For the familiar white Sancerre style, which grape should you expect?

options.text: Riesling
Sémillon
Sauvignon Blanc
Chardonnay

mcqs.explanation: White Sancerre is a Loire Sauvignon Blanc wine; the Sancerre appellation also produces Pinot Noir red and rosé wines.

mcqs.prompt: Which pairing identifies the familiar Chablis wine?

options.text: Rhône Viognier
Northern Burgundy Chardonnay
Loire Chenin Blanc
Alsace Gewurztraminer

mcqs.explanation: Chablis is a Chardonnay white wine from northern Burgundy, commonly showing citrus or green-apple fruit and a fresh, taut character.

mcqs.prompt: Which is the central grape in the beginner white Burgundy example?

options.text: Chardonnay
Sauvignon Blanc
Albariño
Furmint

mcqs.explanation: Chardonnay is the central white Burgundy example. Styles differ from fresh Chablis to fuller Côte de Beaune examples; oak influence varies.

mcqs.prompt: Which is the central grape in the familiar red Burgundy example?

options.text: Gamay
Merlot
Syrah
Pinot Noir

mcqs.explanation: The central red Burgundy example is Pinot Noir, commonly showing red-fruit character; site, vintage, extraction and maturation affect the finished style.

mcqs.prompt: Which pair is central to the familiar red Bordeaux blend?

options.text: Grenache and Tempranillo
Nebbiolo and Barbera
Merlot and Cabernet Sauvignon
Gamay and Pinot Noir

mcqs.explanation: Red Bordeaux commonly combines Merlot fruit and supple texture with Cabernet Sauvignon tannic structure; proportions and wine styles vary.

mcqs.prompt: Where do the bubbles develop in the familiar Champagne production method?

options.text: From sugar added just before each glass is served
During a second fermentation in bottle
Through a still-wine cork reacting with acid
By boiling a finished wine in open pans

mcqs.explanation: Champagne is a sparkling wine from Champagne in France, with bubbles developed through a second fermentation in the bottle.

mcqs.prompt: Which description identifies the familiar Sauternes style?

options.text: Sweet white Bordeaux, usually based on Sémillon
Dry red Burgundy based on Pinot Noir
Dry fortified Palomino
Fresh Italian sparkling Glera

mcqs.explanation: Sauternes is a sweet white Bordeaux wine, usually based on Sémillon with supporting varieties such as Sauvignon Blanc.

mcqs.prompt: A customer chooses the familiar commercial White Zinfandel. Which expectation should you clarify?

options.text: It is necessarily a dry white made from white grapes
It is a traditional-method sparkling wine
It is a naturally fortified black wine
It is commonly a noticeably sweet rosé style

mcqs.explanation: White Zinfandel is a blush or rosé style made from Zinfandel; the familiar commercial example has noticeable sweetness despite the word White.

mcqs.prompt: Which grape makes the familiar red Beaujolais example?

options.text: Cabernet Sauvignon
Nebbiolo
Gamay
Pinot Noir

mcqs.explanation: Red Beaujolais is made from Gamay, commonly with fresh red fruit and relatively gentle tannins, although structure differs across wines and sites.

mcqs.prompt: Which description fits the familiar red Côtes du Rhône example?

options.text: A sweet German Riesling
A still Rhône red, often involving Grenache and Syrah
A sparkling Loire white made by tank fermentation
A fortified Burgundy red

mcqs.explanation: The familiar red Côtes du Rhône example is a still red Rhône wine, often blended from varieties including Grenache and Syrah; white and rosé also exist.

mcqs.prompt: Which grape is central to the familiar Tuscan Chianti example?

options.text: Sangiovese
Nebbiolo
Corvina
Montepulciano

mcqs.explanation: Chianti is a Tuscan red wine centred on Sangiovese; accompanying varieties and maturation produce different expressions.

mcqs.prompt: Which grape is especially associated with the familiar red Rioja example?

options.text: Nebbiolo
Carménère
Gamay
Tempranillo

mcqs.explanation: Tempranillo is especially associated with red Rioja. Rioja offers young fruit-focused reds and matured styles, as well as other wine colours.

mcqs.prompt: Which region and style fit the familiar red Châteauneuf-du-Pape example?

options.text: Piedmont sweet white
Eastern Germany fortified red
Southern Rhône still red
Northern Loire sparkling white

mcqs.explanation: The familiar Châteauneuf-du-Pape example is a southern Rhône still red wine involving black grapes such as Grenache; the appellation also makes still white wine.

mcqs.prompt: Which grape and wine type form the usual familiar Prosecco example?

options.text: Sémillon-based sweet Bordeaux white
Glera-based Italian sparkling wine
Chardonnay-based fortified wine
Pinot Noir-based Spanish still red

mcqs.explanation: The usual Prosecco example is an Italian sparkling wine based on Glera. Semi-sparkling and still Prosecco styles also exist, and sweetness varies.

mcqs.prompt: Which description fits Cava?

options.text: Spanish traditional-method sparkling wine
Portuguese wine fortified during fermentation
German ancestral-method still wine
French force-carbonated red wine

mcqs.explanation: Cava is a Spanish sparkling wine made using the traditional method, in which the second fermentation occurs in the bottle.

mcqs.prompt: A bottle is labelled Sherry without a sweetness description. Which statement is justified?

options.text: Every Sherry must be very sweet
Every Sherry is a still unfortified rosé
The name alone proves residual sugar is absent
Sherry includes both dry and sweet styles

mcqs.explanation: Sherry includes dry fortified styles and naturally sweet or blended sweet styles; the Sherry name alone does not specify its sweetness.

mcqs.prompt: Which statement about Port avoids a common beginner mistake?

options.text: Its bubbles require bottle fermentation
Its sweetness comes only from adding sugar at service
It is fortified during fermentation and is not exclusively red
It is always a dry white wine

mcqs.explanation: Port is fortified during fermentation with grape spirit. Familiar red Ports are sweet, but Port also occurs in white and other colour and sweetness styles.

mcqs.prompt: Which Chardonnay expectation is most useful for a beginner?

options.text: Chardonnay is a black grape used only for reds
White styles range from fresh and lighter to fuller, with oak depending on production
Every Chardonnay must taste strongly of new oak
Every Chardonnay is a sweet sparkling wine

mcqs.explanation: Chardonnay produces white wines ranging from fresh, lighter examples to fuller wines with ripe fruit; oak influence depends on winemaking.

mcqs.prompt: Which is a common beginner Sauvignon Blanc profile?

options.text: Aromatic white with high acidity and possible citrus or herbal notes
Low-acid red with firm tannin
Dry fortified wine with obligatory flor
A full red whose only aroma comes from oak

mcqs.explanation: Sauvignon Blanc commonly makes aromatic, high-acid white wine; citrus, green fruit and herbs can occur, with riper tropical fruit in some examples.

mcqs.prompt: How are Pinot Grigio and Pinot Gris related?

options.text: They are two varieties separated by wine sweetness
One is white wine and the other is a black-grape species
They are names for sparkling production methods
They are names for the same grape variety

mcqs.explanation: Pinot Grigio and Pinot Gris name the same variety. Familiar Italian examples are often fresh and fruity, while Alsace examples can be richer and fuller.

mcqs.prompt: Which statement describes the range of Riesling styles?

options.text: Riesling is a high-tannin red
Dry Riesling cannot have citrus aromas
High-acid whites can be dry, off-dry or sweet
Riesling is necessarily sweet

mcqs.explanation: Riesling commonly makes light- to medium-bodied, high-acid white wine with citrus aromas. It can be dry, off-dry or sweet.

mcqs.prompt: Which is a common Cabernet Sauvignon red-wine profile?

options.text: Low-acid fortified wine with flor
Black fruit with noticeable tannic structure
Rose and lychee with no tannin in a white wine
Only sweet pink wine with bubbles

mcqs.explanation: Cabernet Sauvignon commonly gives medium- to full-bodied red wine with black-fruit aromas and noticeable tannic structure; ripeness and region affect the balance.

mcqs.prompt: Which fruit and texture combination is common in Merlot?

options.text: Plum or cherry and a rounded texture
Lemon and strongly saline white-wine flavour
Lychee and a compulsory sweet finish
Only dried-fruit aromas produced by flor

mcqs.explanation: Merlot commonly makes red wine with plum or cherry fruit and a rounded texture; examples range from lighter wines to dense, structured styles.

mcqs.prompt: Which is a common beginner Pinot Noir profile?

options.text: Full-bodied white with no acidity
Sweet fortified red made only from dried grapes
A grape whose wine must have powerful new-oak flavour
Light- to medium-bodied red with cherry or strawberry

mcqs.explanation: Pinot Noir commonly makes light- to medium-bodied red wine with cherry or strawberry aromas. Extraction, ripeness and maturation change its structure.

mcqs.prompt: Which statement correctly links Syrah and Shiraz?

options.text: Shiraz denotes added grape spirit rather than a grape
Syrah means all wine was fermented in bottle
They name the same black grape, whose wines vary by site and method
They are unrelated grapes with different berry colours

mcqs.explanation: Syrah and Shiraz are names for the same black grape. Wines can show dark fruit and pepper or spice, with body varying by region and method.

mcqs.prompt: A grower is assessing harvest ripeness. Which set of juice measures is useful alongside taste?

options.text: Only the vineyard’s retail price
Sugar, pH and titratable acidity
Bottle pressure, cork length and dosage
Only the finished wine’s tannin

mcqs.explanation: Growers measure juice sugar, pH and titratable acidity alongside taste and other indicators; sugar alone does not describe complete fruit maturity.

mcqs.prompt: The root zone is too dry and vine growth is slowing severely. What does irrigation supply?

options.text: Water
Fermentable sugar to grape skins
Carbon dioxide bubbles to the future wine
Oak tannin to the roots

mcqs.explanation: Irrigation supplies water when available soil moisture is insufficient. Severe water shortage can greatly slow vine growth; needs depend on site and conditions.

mcqs.prompt: Which approach to fertilisation best follows vine and site needs?

options.text: Use the largest available dose in every block
Use grape sweetness alone to choose fertiliser
Replace all soil assessment with bottle tasting
Assess the vine and site before choosing additions

mcqs.explanation: Mineral nutrients support normal vine growth. Site and plant assessments guide additions rather than assuming more fertiliser always improves the crop.

mcqs.prompt: A berry begins to soften and change colour after fruit set. Which stage has begun?

options.text: Alcoholic fermentation
Fruit set before flowering
Veraison
Winter pruning

mcqs.explanation: Veraison marks the onset of berry ripening, including softening and colour change; it follows flowering and fruit set.

mcqs.prompt: Dense cold air tends to collect around a frost-prone block. Which site feature can help it move away?

options.text: An opaque bottle
Suitable air-draining slope
A depression that traps cold air
A permanently enclosed cellar

mcqs.explanation: A site with good air drainage lets dense cold air move away rather than collect around vines; local terrain still determines the frost risk.

mcqs.prompt: An excessively dense canopy restricts airflow and drying. Which response addresses that mechanism?

options.text: Appropriate shoot and leaf management
Increase shading in every part of the canopy
Add spirit to the roots
Ignore fruit exposure in disease management

mcqs.explanation: A dense canopy restricts airflow and shades fruit. Suitable shoot and leaf management improves exposure and drying while avoiding overexposure.

mcqs.prompt: A large crop exceeds the vine’s functional leaf capacity. Which consequence is plausible?

options.text: Instant ripening irrespective of photosynthesis
A guaranteed improvement in every wine quality
Automatic elimination of disease risk
Delayed balanced maturity and depleted vine reserves

mcqs.explanation: An excessive crop relative to functional leaf area can delay balanced maturity and deplete vine reserves; yield alone does not establish wine quality.

mcqs.prompt: Why is an extra week of hang time not automatically a quality improvement?

options.text: It prevents fruit sugar and acid from changing
It removes the need to assess the intended style
It can add exposure to late rain, disease and dehydration
It eliminates all predators from the vineyard

mcqs.explanation: Longer hang time may develop flavour but increases exposure to disease, predators, late rain or frost and berry dehydration.

mcqs.prompt: For a delicate white style, which aim supports gentle handling and prompt pressing?

options.text: Add new-oak aroma without wood contact
Limit unwanted phenolic extraction
Maximise all possible skin tannin
Produce gas through a second bottle fermentation

mcqs.explanation: Gentle handling and prompt pressing can limit phenolic extraction for a delicate white style; longer contact may be chosen for other styles.

mcqs.prompt: Damaging bunch rot is present in fruit for a fresh dry wine. What should selective picking or sorting limit?

options.text: Mould-affected material entering the winery
All healthy berries of the same variety
Only tartrate crystals after bottling
Only the size of clean fermentation tanks

mcqs.explanation: Where damaging Botrytis bunch rot is present, selective picking or sorting limits mould-affected material entering the winery. This is distinct from intentionally using suitable noble-rot fruit.

mcqs.prompt: Why keep white free-run and press fractions separate initially?

options.text: To prove each fraction uses a different grape variety
To guarantee all press fractions are sweeter
To remove the need for tasting the final blend
To assess their differing phenolic character before blending

mcqs.explanation: Processing free-run and press fractions separately allows the winemaker to assess and manage different phenolic characters before blending for the intended white-wine style.

mcqs.prompt: What can controlled contact between white-grape juice and skins contribute?

options.text: Flavour and texture through extraction; excessive contact can add astringency
A guarantee that every white wine becomes sweet
Removal of every aroma compound from the juice
Carbon dioxide added without any extraction

mcqs.explanation: Contact between juice and white-grape skins can increase flavour and texture through extraction; excessive contact can also bring astringency or herbaceous character.

mcqs.prompt: Varying red-fermentation cap contact most directly influences what?

options.text: The cork’s thickness
Colour and tannin extraction
The grape’s original DNA identity
The appellation boundary

mcqs.explanation: The extent and duration of contact between fermenting red must and the cap influence the extraction of colour and tannin. More intensive treatment is not automatically preferable.

mcqs.prompt: What stylistic aim can cooler fermentation support in an aromatic white?

options.text: Preservation of delicate aroma character
Maximum new-oak extraction without wood
Conversion of all malic acid by yeast
Elimination of any need for healthy yeast

mcqs.explanation: Cooler fermentation can help preserve delicate white-wine aroma character. The temperature still has to suit the yeast and allow reliable fermentation.

mcqs.prompt: What happens during malolactic conversion?

options.text: Grape sugar becomes alcohol and carbon dioxide
Tannin becomes grape pigment
Ethanol is added to stop fermentation
Malic acid becomes lactic acid, reducing acidity

mcqs.explanation: Lactic acid bacteria convert L-malic acid into L-lactic acid during MLF, reducing acidity. This is a different process from yeast converting sugars into alcohol.

mcqs.prompt: Compared with new barrels, repeated use commonly changes which contribution?

options.text: Mandatory creation of bubbles
Complete absence of any maturation influence
Less freshly extractable oak character
More grape sugar extracted from the wood

mcqs.explanation: Repeated barrel use reduces the distinction in extractable oak character compared with new wood. Used barrels can still influence maturation and require care.

mcqs.prompt: Managed yeast-lees contact can alter which wine feature?

options.text: Whether the skins were black or white
Texture and flavour integration
The grape variety’s identity
The geographical origin of the vineyard

mcqs.explanation: During lees contact, yeast-derived compounds including polysaccharides and mannoproteins can alter texture and flavour integration. Results depend on management and time.

mcqs.prompt: A white wine is susceptible to protein haze. Which instability does bentonite address?

options.text: Susceptible proteins
Dissolved carbon dioxide alone
Grape sugar needed for tirage
Sediment caused solely by red pigment ageing

mcqs.explanation: Negatively charged bentonite binds susceptible proteins, helping remove material that could form a later haze. The effective addition depends on the particular wine.

mcqs.prompt: Which contrast fits Chardonnay grown at cooler versus warmer sites?

options.text: Cooler examples must be red and warmer examples white
Climate cannot affect Chardonnay fruit character
Warmer sites guarantee sweet fortified wine
Cooler examples often show citrus and higher acidity; warmer examples can be riper and fuller

mcqs.explanation: Cool-site Chardonnay commonly shows citrus or green fruit and higher acidity; warmer-site examples can show riper fruit and fuller body.

mcqs.prompt: A cooler New Zealand Sauvignon Blanc is being described. Which combination is a familiar tendency?

options.text: Strong red colour and rose-like tannin
Flor-derived acetaldehyde with no fruit aromas
High acidity with gooseberry or capsicum
Very low acidity with compulsory dried-grape sweetness

mcqs.explanation: Cooler New Zealand Sauvignon Blanc often combines high acidity with gooseberry or capsicum; warmer-site examples may be fuller and show melon or stone fruit.

mcqs.prompt: Which contrast fits fresh northeastern Italian Pinot Grigio and fuller Alsace Pinot Gris?

options.text: Italian examples cannot show fruit aromas
The same variety can yield markedly different weights and aroma profiles
The different names prove unrelated varieties
Alsace examples must be sparkling

mcqs.explanation: Fresh northeastern Italian Pinot Grigio contrasts with fuller Alsace Pinot Gris, which can show dried apricot, honey, smoky or spicy notes.

mcqs.prompt: A dry Australian Riesling has intense lemon and lime fruit. What should a taster avoid inferring from aroma alone?

options.text: That the wine must taste sweet
That it can have high acidity
That it is a white wine
That it may have citrus aromas

mcqs.explanation: Australian Riesling commonly has high acidity and lemon or lime aromas; a dry wine need not taste sweet despite its fruit intensity.

mcqs.prompt: Which combination suits the cited Coonawarra Cabernet Sauvignon profile?

options.text: Lychee and rose with a low-tannin white palate
Delicate lemon in a pale dry white
Yeast-derived bubbles and sweet dosage
Blackcurrant or plum with firm tannin

mcqs.explanation: Coonawarra Cabernet commonly combines blackcurrant or plum with firm tannins; Margaret River examples can show blackcurrant, cedar and violet.

mcqs.prompt: Which claim about Bordeaux Merlot allows for different production levels?

options.text: Merlot fruit character proves every wine is sweet
Merlot must be blended with Pinot Noir
Supple cherry or plum styles can also become concentrated, ageworthy wines
Merlot cannot make powerful wines

mcqs.explanation: Bordeaux Merlot commonly combines moderate acidity with cherry, plum or fig and supple texture; greater concentration can support a powerful ageworthy style.

mcqs.prompt: Which profile is common in cool Australian Pinot Noir?

options.text: A full red whose tannin level never changes
Cherry or strawberry in a light- to medium-bodied red
A white wine dominated by lychee
A fortified wine defined by flor

mcqs.explanation: Cool Australian Pinot Noir commonly shows cherry or strawberry and a light to medium body; site and winemaking affect flavour concentration and texture.

mcqs.prompt: Which style can occur in warm Barossa Shiraz?

options.text: Blackberry and spice with substantial body
A mandatory light, sweet white wine
A compulsory low-alcohol fortified rosé
Only lemon and lime with no red colour

mcqs.explanation: Shiraz body varies from medium to full; warm Barossa examples can show blackberry and spice, while other regions give less weight or more savoury character.

mcqs.prompt: Which tendency is common in Beaujolais Gamay?

options.text: Very low acidity and obligatory heavy new oak
A white wine with rose and lychee
A wine whose tannin is fixed by law in every site
Fresh red fruit and delicate tannin, with some more structured examples

mcqs.explanation: Beaujolais Gamay commonly shows red fruit, freshness and delicate tannin; some sites produce more structured examples.

mcqs.prompt: What can Grenache Noir contribute to a dry Rhône red?

options.text: The bubbles of a tank fermentation without yeast
A white colour forced by the variety name
Ripe red fruit and supple texture
Obligatory residual sweetness from every grape

mcqs.explanation: Grenache Noir can give ripe red-fruit character and a supple texture in dry Rhône reds; ripeness, blending and extraction affect weight and structure.

mcqs.prompt: How may a young Rioja Tempranillo differ from a matured example?

options.text: Young Rioja cannot show plum or strawberry
Young fruit can be joined by vanilla, cocoa or liquorice after maturation
Ageing makes every Tempranillo sparkling
Maturation necessarily removes all fruit and tannin

mcqs.explanation: Young Rioja Tempranillo can show plum, strawberry or floral notes; matured examples can add vanilla, cocoa or liquorice from maturation.

mcqs.prompt: Which structural judgement is sound for a modestly coloured Piedmont Nebbiolo?

options.text: Substantial tannin and acidity can coexist with modest colour
Pale colour proves the absence of tannin
Only deep colour allows noticeable acidity
Nebbiolo colour fixes the wine’s residual sugar

mcqs.explanation: Piedmont Nebbiolo commonly combines substantial tannin and acidity with rose, dried cherry or earthy notes; modest colour does not imply weak structure.

mcqs.prompt: Which tendency is characteristic of Barbera?

options.text: All Barbera must be white
Oak maturation is incompatible with Barbera
High acidity necessarily makes the wine sweet
Notable acidity, with styles ranging from fresh to richer wood-matured wines

mcqs.explanation: Barbera retains notable acidity and colour; it can make fresh medium-bodied wine or richer, ripe wines suitable for wood maturation.

mcqs.prompt: Which structure is often found in Tuscan Sangiovese?

options.text: A low-tannin white palate with citrus only
Bubbles caused by flor ageing
Bright acidity and defined tannin with cherry or plum
No acidity and compulsory sweet dosage

mcqs.explanation: Tuscan Sangiovese often combines bright acidity and defined tannin with cherry or plum; wood maturation can add vanilla, coffee or tobacco impressions.

mcqs.prompt: Which description fits Corvina in young Valpolicella?

options.text: A black grape whose every wine must be dried-grape fortified
Fresh dry red blends with cherry and delicate fruit or floral notes
A sweet white Tokaj wine
A wine defined by mandatory bubbles

mcqs.explanation: In young Valpolicella, Corvina contributes to fresh dry red blends showing cherry and delicate fruit or floral notes; production affects structure.

mcqs.prompt: Which profile fits the cited Montepulciano d’Abruzzo example?

options.text: A full red with fruit, spice and noticeable tannin
A light white with only citrus and no structure
A sparkling Glera wine
A dry flor-aged fortified wine

mcqs.explanation: Montepulciano d’Abruzzo provides a full, harmonious red-wine example with red-fruit and spice aromas and noticeable tannin; maturation changes colour and aroma.

mcqs.prompt: Which description allows for the range of red Zinfandel?

options.text: All examples have identical alcohol and tannin
Every Zinfandel must be white and dry
The grape name requires bottle fermentation
Weight and ripeness vary; blackberry and pepper can occur

mcqs.explanation: Red Zinfandel styles vary in weight and ripeness; Sonoma examples commonly show blackberry with pepper or other spices.

mcqs.prompt: Which expectation allows for different Pinotage winemaking choices?

options.text: Every Pinotage must be sweet rosé
Pinotage can only be made with flor
Berry or plum reds can vary in texture and oak expression
The variety guarantees smoky oak aroma in every wine

mcqs.explanation: Pinotage red wines can show berry or plum aromas; fruit expression, extraction and oak use produce varied textures and aromas.

mcqs.prompt: Which is a familiar Chilean Carménère tendency?

options.text: A grape whose tannin must be extremely high in every wine
Dry red with ripe dark fruit and possible herbal or pepper notes
Sparkling white with mandatory dosage
Sweet white with no acidity

mcqs.explanation: Chilean Carménère commonly makes dry, medium- to full-bodied red wine with ripe dark fruit and herbaceous or pepper notes; tannin is often moderate.

mcqs.prompt: Which profile can occur in Argentine Malbec?

options.text: Ripe fruit, floral aromas and substantial body, with freshness varying by site
A white wine whose acidity never changes
Only a light sweet rosé with no tannin
A red requiring spirit addition by definition

mcqs.explanation: Argentine Malbec can show ripe fruit and floral aromas with substantial body; cooler elevated sites can retain freshness and different tannin textures.

mcqs.prompt: Which combination captures Chenin Blanc’s range?

options.text: Only sweet still wine with little acidity
Only dry red wines
A grape whose name fixes oak use
Assertive acidity with dry or sweet, still or sparkling styles

mcqs.explanation: Chenin Blanc has assertive acidity and can produce dry or sweet, still or sparkling white wine; oak, ripeness and botrytis change its expression.

mcqs.prompt: An aged Hunter Valley Sémillon smells of toast. What should be considered before concluding that oak was used?

options.text: Every Sémillon is made in new barrels
Dry Sémillon cannot have bottle-derived aromas
Bottle age can bring toast or honey without requiring oak
Toast proves the grape was black

mcqs.explanation: Young Hunter Valley Sémillon commonly shows lemon and high acidity in a light-bodied dry style; bottle age can bring honey or toast without requiring oak.

mcqs.prompt: A dry Rhône Viognier has a rich, creamy texture. Which inference should be avoided?

options.text: That a dry style is possible
That richness proves residual sweetness
That the wine can show yellow-fruit aromas
That wine texture can be supple

mcqs.explanation: Dry Rhône Viognier can show yellow fruit, spice or dried-fruit aromas and a creamy, supple texture; richness of texture does not establish sweetness.

mcqs.prompt: Which profile is common in Alsace Gewurztraminer?

options.text: Pronounced rose, lychee or spice with full body
A tannic red with only blackcurrant
A wine defined by bottle fermentation
A grape whose wines must all be strongly acidic and light

mcqs.explanation: Alsace Gewurztraminer commonly shows pronounced rose, lychee or spice, with full body and less prominent freshness than many other Alsace white styles.

mcqs.prompt: Which aroma set can occur in Marche Verdicchio?

options.text: Only blackcurrant and firm red-wine tannin
Mandatory flor-derived acetaldehyde
Only aromas from added apple juice
White fruit, citrus, flowers and almond

mcqs.explanation: Marche Verdicchio can show white-fleshed fruit, citrus, flowers and almond, with freshness and structure varying by site and production style.

mcqs.prompt: Which is a familiar Gavi Cortese profile?

options.text: Full red with compulsory dried grape fruit
Sparkling rosé defined by a second bottle fermentation
Dry and fresh, with white fruit, flowers or citrus
Sweet fortified red with flor

mcqs.explanation: Gavi Cortese commonly offers a dry, fresh palate with white fruit, flowers, citrus or bitter-almond notes; richer ageworthy versions also occur.

mcqs.prompt: Which aroma set can occur in Garganega-based Soave?

options.text: Only yeast aromas from a second fermentation
Fruit, white flowers and almond
Only red cherry and powerful black-grape tannin
Compulsory vanilla from every vineyard

mcqs.explanation: Garganega-based Soave can show fruit, white flowers and almond; texture and flavour intensity depend on site, ripeness and winemaking.

mcqs.prompt: Which tendency fits Fiano di Avellino?

options.text: Marked acidity with white fruit or flowers and possible hazelnut
A red with low acidity and only plum
A wine necessarily sweet because of nutty aroma
A sparkling wine requiring force carbonation

mcqs.explanation: Fiano di Avellino commonly has marked acidity, medium structure, white fruit or flowers and a hazelnut note; examples change with maturation.

mcqs.prompt: Which tendency fits Rías Baixas Albariño?

options.text: A tannic red defined by rose aromas
A low-acid sweet fortified wine
A wine whose fruit aromas prove added peaches
Natural acidity with citrus, peach or apricot and floral aromas

mcqs.explanation: Rías Baixas Albariño commonly combines natural acidity with citrus, peach or apricot and floral aromas; fruit profile and texture vary.

mcqs.prompt: Which structure is often observed in Furmint and is relevant when assessing its sweet examples?

options.text: A compulsory tannic red-wine palate
Mandatory bubbles from carbon dioxide injection
High acidity and relatively full body
Little acidity and no body

mcqs.explanation: Furmint often combines high acidity and relatively full body with quince, peach or apricot; it can make dry and botrytis-affected sweet wines.

mcqs.prompt: A Chardonnay producer wants added texture without necessarily using new oak. Which choice can help?

options.text: Adding spirit solely to create dry texture
Managed lees contact
Changing the wine’s geographical origin after harvest
Removing every dissolved aroma compound

mcqs.explanation: Oak contact can add aroma, malolactic conversion can soften the acid impression, and lees contact can add texture; Chardonnay producers use these choices selectively.

mcqs.prompt: Why can retained acidity matter in a sweeter Riesling?

options.text: It can balance perceived sweetness
It converts all residual sugar into tannin
It guarantees the wine is dry
It removes the influence of site and ripeness

mcqs.explanation: Australian Riesling is often dry, but off-dry and sweet wines also occur; retained acidity balances sweetness, and some examples evolve in bottle.

mcqs.prompt: What can Cabernet Sauvignon add to a supple Merlot-led blend?

options.text: The absence of alcoholic fermentation
A mandatory sparkling finish
A change from grape wine to apple wine
A firmer tannic backbone

mcqs.explanation: Merlot styles range from light, juicy reds to powerful wines. Blending with Cabernet Sauvignon can add a firmer tannic backbone to its supple fruit.

mcqs.prompt: Why should a producer assess oak intensity carefully in a delicately fruited Pinot Noir?

options.text: Oak always guarantees more balanced Pinot Noir
Pinot Noir colour proves oak is absent
Excessive oak can overwhelm the fruit
Oak cannot influence any red wine

mcqs.explanation: Pinot Noir producers vary whole-bunch inclusion, extraction and oak. These choices change aroma and tannic structure; delicate fruit can be overwhelmed by excessive oak.

mcqs.prompt: What stylistic aim can whole-berry or carbonic techniques support in some Beaujolais?

options.text: A wine with no fermentation-derived alcohol
Youthful fruit expression
Mandatory long oxidative Tawny maturation
A flor-aged dry fortified style

mcqs.explanation: Some Beaujolais Gamay uses whole-berry or carbonic techniques that emphasise youthful fruit; vineyard, extraction and maturation still create diverse styles.

mcqs.prompt: Which range demonstrates that Grenache Noir does not fix sweetness or colour by itself?

options.text: Dry red and rosé as well as sweet fortified styles
Only one dry red style
Only unfermented white juice
Only force-carbonated wines

mcqs.explanation: Grenache Noir is used for dry red and rosé Rhône wines and for sweet fortified wines; grape identity alone does not determine sweetness or colour.

mcqs.prompt: How can drying grapes change a Corvina-based Amarone compared with young Valpolicella?

options.text: Drying requires the finished wine to remain sweet
Drying turns the grape into Sauvignon Blanc
Drying eliminates the need for fermentation
It can yield a dry wine with higher alcohol and greater structure

mcqs.explanation: Corvina-based blends range from fresh young Valpolicella to Amarone from dried grapes; drying and fermentation can yield a dry wine with higher alcohol and structure.

mcqs.prompt: Which comparison shows that a black grape can produce different wine styles?

options.text: White Zinfandel and dry white Riesling as the same variety
Two wines whose colours are fixed by their bottle glass
Fruit-rich red Zinfandel and sweet blush White Zinfandel
Only red wines from all Zinfandel fruit

mcqs.explanation: Zinfandel can make fruit-rich red wine or the familiar sweet White Zinfandel blush style; grape colour does not force one wine colour or sweetness.

mcqs.prompt: Why are dry ripening periods relevant to Chilean Carménère?

options.text: They remove all herbaceous compounds by definition
The late-ripening variety needs suitable conditions to reach maturity
They replace the need for any vine water
They ensure every wine is identical

mcqs.explanation: Carménère is late ripening. Chilean sites with dry ripening periods can support maturity; its regional expressions can show different fruit and spice balances.

mcqs.prompt: Which fruit choice can contribute to a concentrated honeyed Chenin Blanc style?

options.text: Late-picked or suitable botrytis-affected fruit
Only unripe berries with no sugar
Only fruit of another named variety
Only adding honey after service

mcqs.explanation: Chenin Blanc can be unoaked or oaked, still or sparkling, dry or sweet. Late-picked or botrytis-affected fruit can produce a concentrated honeyed style.

mcqs.prompt: What production distinction helps explain dry Soave versus sweet Recioto di Soave?

options.text: Changing Garganega into a black variety
Required injection of carbon dioxide into both
A law requiring all Soave to have identical sweetness
Fruit drying and fermentation choices

mcqs.explanation: Garganega is associated with dry Soave and dried-grape sweet Recioto di Soave; fruit drying and fermentation choices change concentration and sweetness.

mcqs.prompt: What can malolactic conversion do in an Albariño style when the producer chooses it?

options.text: Create a second alcoholic fermentation in bottle
Require every Rías Baixas wine to be sweet
Contribute to a rounder acid impression
Change Albariño into Chardonnay

mcqs.explanation: Rías Baixas producers can retain acidity or use malolactic conversion for a rounder style; lees contact and selected oak use also change Albariño texture.

mcqs.prompt: Which storage approach best protects unopened wine?

options.text: A hot shelf under direct light
Cool, stable temperature
Repeated heating and chilling
Long-term placement beside a heater

mcqs.explanation: Keep unopened wine cool and at a stable temperature; prolonged heat or large temperature swings can damage it.

mcqs.prompt: Which bottle-position advice distinguishes conventional cork and screwcap still wines?

options.text: Cork bottles can lie on their sides; screwcaps can stand upright
Every screwcap must stay in contact with wine
Cork bottles require freezing before storage
Bottle closure never affects storage position

mcqs.explanation: For conventional cork-closed still wines, side storage maintains cork contact with wine; screwcaps can stand upright.

mcqs.prompt: Which approximate service range is suggested for a full-bodied red?
mcqs.explanation: Use roughly 15–18°C for full-bodied reds; a heated room above this range is not the intended service condition.

mcqs.prompt: Which approximate range suits a lightly chilled fuller white?
mcqs.explanation: A fuller-bodied white can be lightly chilled around 10–13°C; extreme cold masks aroma and flavour.

mcqs.prompt: Why add water as well as ice to a chilling bucket?

options.text: The water converts residual sugar into gas
Cold water improves contact and heat transfer around the bottle
Water adds alcohol through the glass
Air gaps transfer heat faster than cold water

mcqs.explanation: Use both ice and water: contact with cold water transfers heat more effectively than gaps of air between ice cubes.

mcqs.prompt: What should be checked before pouring a sample for judgement?

options.text: Glasses are clean and odour-free
The glass has the strongest detergent aroma
The glass contains yesterday’s wine residue
The rim has deliberately added sweet flavour

mcqs.explanation: Use clean, odour-free glasses so residues do not distort the wine.

mcqs.prompt: You are loosening the wire on a sparkling bottle. Which action is essential?

options.text: Release the cork and aim upwards through a crowd
Shake the bottle to make opening easier
Warm the bottle beside a heater
Keep a firm hand on the cork and point away from people

mcqs.explanation: Keep a firm hand on the cork while loosening the wire; point the bottle away from people.

mcqs.prompt: How should a restrained sparkling cork be eased out?

options.text: Pull sharply while aiming at another person
Shake vigorously before rotating the cork
Gently rotate the bottle while controlling the cork
Let the cork fly freely as soon as the wire is loose

mcqs.explanation: Restrain the cork and gently rotate the bottle; ease the cork out without letting it fly.

mcqs.prompt: How can opened still red wine be protected between services?

options.text: Assume red wine cannot oxidise
Reclose and refrigerate it
Leave it open beside a warm oven
Expose it to strong sunlight

mcqs.explanation: Reclose opened still wine and refrigerate it, including red wine; cooling slows oxidation.

mcqs.prompt: Which method helps preserve an opened sparkling bottle?

options.text: A suitable sparkling stopper and cool storage
A spoon placed in the neck
An unsealed warm decanter
A still-wine vacuum pump operated until gas stops escaping

mcqs.explanation: Use a purpose-made sparkling-wine stopper and keep the opened bottle cool; a spoon in the neck does not preserve bubbles.

mcqs.prompt: Musty aroma and suppressed fruit raise concern about cork-type taint. Which statement is sound?

options.text: A screwcap rules out all cork-type taint
A broken cork alone proves TCA
Strong fruit aroma always proves TCA
TCA can arise even without a cork closure

mcqs.explanation: Cork-type taint may smell musty and suppress fruit; TCA can arise without contact with a cork.

mcqs.prompt: Which statement makes a useful distinction when assessing oxidation?

options.text: All wines must have identical oxidation tolerance
Bottle age alone establishes a fault
Unwanted oxidation can dull fruit, but intentional oxidative styles need their own context
Every sherry-like note proves a spoiled bottle

mcqs.explanation: Unwanted oxidation can dull fruit and introduce stale or sherry-like notes; oxidative styles must be judged in their intended context.

mcqs.prompt: A dry wine is tasted after a clearly sweet pudding. Which perceptual change can occur?

options.text: The wine’s actual sugar content must increase
The wine seems less fruity and more bitter
The pudding chemically removes all wine alcohol
The wine necessarily becomes sparkling

mcqs.explanation: Sweet food can make wine seem less sweet and fruity and more bitter; this is a common perception effect, not a guarantee.

mcqs.prompt: Which starting point is often useful with a sweet dish?

options.text: Trial a wine at least as sweet as the dish
Require the driest available wine in every case
Choose by bottle colour without tasting
Assume sweetness has no effect on perceived balance

mcqs.explanation: For a sweet dish, a wine at least as sweet often preserves balance; check the actual dish, wine and person’s preference.

mcqs.prompt: After an acidic dish, which effect on a wine can occur?

options.text: Its actual alcohol must double
Every wine becomes sweeter through fermentation
The grape variety changes with the food
Its acidity seems softer; a low-acid wine may seem flat

mcqs.explanation: An acidic dish can make wine acidity seem softer; a low-acid wine may then seem flat.

mcqs.prompt: Which common effect can salt have on perceived wine balance?

options.text: Guarantee that any sweet dish works with any wine
Remove all acidity from the liquid
Reduce perceived bitterness and make fruit more evident
Create tannin chemically in the glass

mcqs.explanation: Salt can reduce perceived acidity and bitterness and make fruit more evident; individual sensitivity varies.

mcqs.prompt: A guest wants to avoid increasing chilli burn. Which wine feature deserves particular attention?

options.text: The vineyard’s administrative boundary
Alcohol, which can intensify burning
Bottle glass thickness
The length of the cork

mcqs.explanation: Alcohol can intensify the burning sensation with chilli; a lower-alcohol wine may suit someone seeking gentler heat.

mcqs.prompt: An umami-rich dish makes a tannic trial wine seem bitter and less fruity. What is a sensible next trial?

options.text: A lower-tannin wine with sufficient fruit, checked with the dish
The highest-tannin wine available regardless of preference
A hotter glass of the same wine without tasting
A choice based only on the meat’s colour

mcqs.explanation: With pronounced umami, consider lower tannin and sufficient fruit intensity, then check acidity, salt and the actual pairing.

mcqs.prompt: What is the primary sediment-related purpose of gently decanting an older red?

options.text: Increase residual sugar
Convert the wine to a sparkling style
Prove the wine needed several hours of aeration
Separate clear wine from deposit

mcqs.explanation: Some aged or less-filtered reds form a deposit; gentle decanting separates clear wine from sediment.

mcqs.prompt: Which claim should a wine professional avoid?

options.text: That an alcohol-free option may suit a guest
That wine quality and alcohol-related risk are different matters
That expensive wine is a risk-free health choice
That wine contains ethanol

mcqs.explanation: Expensive or high-quality wine still contains ethanol; do not present wine as a treatment or a risk-free health choice.

mcqs.prompt: In traditional-method sparkling wine, where is the second alcoholic fermentation carried out?

options.text: Inside the cork
In bottle
In the vineyard berries
Only in an open decanter

mcqs.explanation: The traditional method creates its second alcoholic fermentation in bottle, retaining the fermentation gas in the wine.

mcqs.prompt: Which addition supplies the ingredients for a second fermentation in dry base wine?

options.text: Sugar and yeast in tirage
Only oak tannin
Only grape spirit
Only bentonite

mcqs.explanation: Tirage supplies fermentable sugar and yeast to the base wine; this differs from sweetness adjustment after disgorgement.

mcqs.prompt: Where does conventional tank-method sparkling wine undergo its second fermentation?

options.text: In individual bottles followed by riddling
In open trays of drying grapes
In a flor-ageing butt without gas retention
In a sealed pressure tank

mcqs.explanation: In the conventional tank method, sugar and yeast initiate a second fermentation in a sealed tank that retains the gas.

mcqs.prompt: An ancestral sparkling wine is bottled before the original fermentation ends. Where do its bubbles come from?

options.text: Disgorgement converting yeast into gas
The colour extracted from black skins
Continuing fermentation of remaining grape sugar in bottle
A compulsory separate tirage fermentation after dryness

mcqs.explanation: In an ancestral process, the original fermentation continues after bottling, consuming remaining grape sugar and retaining its gas.

mcqs.prompt: What directly provides the gas in force-carbonated wine?

options.text: Fortification with grape spirit
Introduced carbon dioxide
A compulsory new yeast fermentation
Malolactic bacteria converting tannin

mcqs.explanation: Force carbonation introduces carbon dioxide directly into wine rather than generating that gas through a new fermentation.

mcqs.prompt: What is one freshness-related aim of picking fruit for a sparkling base relatively early?

options.text: Retain acidity
Maximise all possible dehydration
Guarantee a sweet finished sparkling wine
Avoid having to assess the intended style

mcqs.explanation: Early picking can retain acidity for a fresh sparkling base, but a useful harvest decision still follows the intended wine style.

mcqs.prompt: Why is a relatively low-alcohol base useful before a planned second fermentation?

options.text: The bottle cork later removes all alcohol
Lees contact automatically halves alcohol
Dosage can only remove alcohol
The second fermentation adds further alcohol

mcqs.explanation: A relatively low-alcohol base allows for alcohol added during second fermentation; the intended final style determines the target.

mcqs.prompt: Which process occurs when dead yeast cells break down during lees ageing?

options.text: Noble rot in unpicked grapes
Distillation of grape spirit
Autolysis
Tirage sugar fermentation by live yeast

mcqs.explanation: Yeast cells break down and release compounds into the wine during autolysis; this differs from active sugar fermentation.

mcqs.prompt: What does riddling prepare for?

options.text: Separation of press fractions before fermentation
Collection of sediment in the neck for removal
Extraction of colour from red skins
Addition of fermentation sugar to vineyard grapes

mcqs.explanation: Riddling rotates and progressively tilts bottles to collect sediment in the neck for later removal.

mcqs.prompt: What does disgorgement remove?

options.text: Lees gathered at the bottle neck
All dissolved carbon dioxide intentionally
The grape’s original sugar before pressing
The base wine’s geographical origin

mcqs.explanation: Opening the prepared bottle expels the lees gathered at its neck; mechanised disgorgement can use a frozen sediment plug.

mcqs.prompt: What can dosage adjust after sparkling-wine sediment removal?

options.text: The berry colour at harvest
The grape variety planted in the vineyard
The timing of the previous harvest
The finishing sweetness profile

mcqs.explanation: Dosage can add wine and sugar after sediment removal, adjusting the finishing profile before final sealing; it is not tirage.

mcqs.prompt: Which statement about MLF in Champagne base wine is correct?

options.text: It is another name for tirage fermentation
It creates carbon dioxide by converting sugar into alcohol
Producers may use, partly conduct or avoid it for their intended style
Every Champagne must complete it

mcqs.explanation: Champagne producers may complete, partly conduct or avoid MLF according to the desired style; it is distinct from alcoholic fermentation.

mcqs.prompt: Why does adding spirit during Port fermentation help retain grape sugar?

options.text: It destroys the grape skins before harvest
It raises alcohol and arrests fermentation before all sugar is consumed
It turns all alcohol back into sugar
It removes sugar by riddling

mcqs.explanation: Spirit raises alcohol and arrests fermentation before all fermentable grape sugar has been consumed.

mcqs.prompt: A producer allows more grape sugar to ferment before Port fortification. What does the timing affect?

options.text: The residual sugar retained
The grape variety’s original identity
Whether the wine came from Portugal
The existence of fermentation carbon dioxide

mcqs.explanation: Adding grape spirit interrupts fermentation; the timing influences how much grape sugar remains.

mcqs.prompt: Which maturation aim fits a fruit-led Ruby-style Port?

options.text: Maximise a Tawny-like oxidative profile
Remove all residual sugar by dosage
Create bottle-fermentation bubbles
Restrain colour evolution and retain young fruit

mcqs.explanation: Ruby-style maturation aims to restrain colour evolution and retain the fruit character of young wine.

mcqs.prompt: Which route develops Tawny colour and dried-fruit character?

options.text: Immediate bottling with no maturation
Pressing frozen grapes without subsequent ageing
Cask maturation
Direct carbon dioxide injection

mcqs.explanation: Cask maturation develops tawny colour and dried-fruit characters; this is a different aim from preserving young Ruby fruit.

mcqs.prompt: Which vessel supports substantial further development of Vintage Port?

options.text: The cork itself, separately from the wine
Bottle
Only a sealed pressure tank for second fermentation
Only an open fermentation trough before fortification

mcqs.explanation: Vintage Port can evolve substantially in bottle; cask-aged Tawny styles are usually prepared for drinking when released.

mcqs.prompt: Which ageing sequence defines Amontillado?

options.text: First under flor, then without flor
Only under flor throughout its entire life
Only without flor from the beginning
Second fermentation in bottle followed by dosage

mcqs.explanation: Amontillado begins with biological ageing and then ages oxidatively after flor disappears. It is dry, amber and nutty, combining a flor-derived foundation with developed aromas. It should not be classified as naturally sweet from its colour or richness.

mcqs.prompt: Why can a rich Oloroso still be dry?

options.text: Its body must be made entirely from residual sugar
Oxidative ageing requires adding dosage sugar
Every fortified wine must be sweet
Its base fermented fully before oxidative ageing; body does not prove sweetness

mcqs.explanation: Oloroso’s oxidative maturation develops amber-to-mahogany colour, nut aromas and a fuller texture. The base is fermented dry; absence of flor preserves more glycerol than in a biologically aged wine. Sweetened blends can use Oloroso, but the dry Oloroso category itself is distinct from Cream.

mcqs.prompt: What does a criaderas-and-solera system do through partial withdrawals and refreshments?

options.text: Keep every bottle tied to a single harvest by definition
Generate bubbles through a second fermentation
Blend wines across successive ageing stages for continuity of style
Completely empty every cask on each withdrawal

mcqs.explanation: Partial withdrawals and refreshments mix wines across successive ageing stages, helping maintain a recognisable house style.

mcqs.prompt: Which comparison correctly distinguishes Cream Sherry from dry Oloroso?

options.text: Cream combines a dry wine with sweetness; dry Oloroso is not its interchangeable name
Cream means every Oloroso must be sweet
Cream is a name for carbon dioxide added to Sherry
Dry Oloroso requires the same sugar as a naturally sweet PX wine

mcqs.explanation: Cream is a sweet blend, often using dry oxidative Oloroso and a naturally sweet component such as PX. It combines mature nutty character with sweetness. PX is instead a naturally sweet raisined-grape wine; dry Oloroso and Cream should not be treated as interchangeable names.

mcqs.prompt: What does mutage achieve in a Vin Doux Naturel?

options.text: Arrest fermentation with wine-derived alcohol while fruit sugar remains
Convert lactic acid back into malic acid
Remove lees by freezing the neck
Create carbonation by injecting oxygen

mcqs.explanation: Adding wine-derived alcohol during fermentation stops yeast before all grape sugar is converted; the sweetness is retained from the fruit.

mcqs.prompt: Which treatment concentrates sugars for the cited Pedro Ximénez Sherry route?

options.text: Pressing only naturally frozen grapes
Picking all grapes before veraison
Removing skin colour through riddling
Drying ripe grapes towards raisins

mcqs.explanation: Asoleo turns ripe Pedro Ximénez grapes towards raisins, concentrating sugars before pressing and a fermentation interrupted by spirit.

mcqs.prompt: How can prolonged Rutherglen Muscat cask maturation affect a producer’s stock?

options.text: It ties up stock and evaporation can reduce saleable volume
It removes all inventory time and evaporation losses
It proves quality solely from the oldest parcel’s age
It replaces oxidative development with a second sparkling fermentation

mcqs.explanation: Cask ageing and evaporation concentrate Rutherglen Muscat while oxidative development brings dried-fruit, caramel and rancio character. Blending young and mature parcels manages freshness and richness. Long-aged stocks require time and lose saleable volume, which can add cost without making age the sole measure of quality.

mcqs.prompt: A French label identifies an AOC/AOP. What does this primarily tell you?

options.text: An estate classification identical to every Bordeaux ranking
A protected delimited origin with a production specification
A grape variety used throughout France
A fixed level of sweetness

mcqs.explanation: For French wine, AOC is the national appellation terminology and AOP is its European protected-origin counterpart. A named appellation has a delimited origin and a production specification; it is not the name of a grape.

mcqs.prompt: Which statement about Pays d’Oc IGP is justified?

options.text: It is a regulated geographical indication with a specification
It is an unregulated synonym for all southern French wine
It guarantees every bottle contains one grape
It means every wine is dry and unoaked

mcqs.explanation: IGP protects a geographical indication linked to origin, reputation or characteristics. It still has a specification; Pays d’Oc is an IGP example, not an unregulated synonym for all southern French wine.

mcqs.prompt: Which pair commonly appears in Bordeaux, Graves and Pessac-Léognan dry whites?

options.text: Riesling and Gewurztraminer
Cortese and Garganega
Furmint and Assyrtiko
Sauvignon Blanc and Sémillon

mcqs.explanation: Bordeaux, Graves and Pessac-Léognan dry whites commonly use Sauvignon Blanc and Sémillon. Cool fermentation can preserve fruit; barrel fermentation or maturation and lees contact can add texture and oak character, so check the cuvée rather than assume every white is oaked.

mcqs.prompt: A label says Saint-Émilion Grand Cru, without Grand Cru Classé. What can you establish?

options.text: That it is a Burgundy Grand Cru vineyard
That all vines grow in one named climat
The appellation, without assuming separately classified estate status
That the estate is necessarily Premier Grand Cru Classé

mcqs.explanation: Saint-Émilion Grand Cru is an appellation. Grand Cru Classé and Premier Grand Cru Classé identify classified estates within that appellation under a separate classification process; a Grand Cru appellation label alone does not establish classified status.

mcqs.prompt: What land must supply an eligible Burgundy village wine labelled Premier Cru?

options.text: Only land within a Grand Cru appellation
Classified Premier Cru sites within the applicable appellation
Any vineyard owned by a classified Bordeaux estate
Any plot anywhere in France planted to Chardonnay

mcqs.explanation: A Burgundy village wine marked Premier Cru comes from classified Premier Cru land. The label may name a particular climat, or indicate a blend from eligible Premier Cru sites within the applicable appellation.

mcqs.prompt: What does Burgundy Grand Cru, such as Chambertin, classify?

options.text: A specific delimited appellation origin
All wines of one estate regardless of origin
A compulsory new-oak programme
The sweetness level of every Pinot Noir

mcqs.explanation: A Burgundy Grand Cru such as Chambertin or Montrachet identifies a specific delimited Grand Cru appellation. It classifies origin rather than every wine made by an estate, which differs from Bordeaux estate classifications.

mcqs.prompt: Where does Bourgogne Côte d’Or belong in the label hierarchy?

options.text: A separate Grand Cru appellation
A Bordeaux estate classification
A synonym for every Côte d’Or village appellation
An additional geographical denomination of regional Bourgogne

mcqs.explanation: Bourgogne Côte d’Or is an additional geographical denomination of the Bourgogne appellation. Its reference to Côte d’Or does not make it a village, Premier Cru or Grand Cru appellation.

mcqs.prompt: Which wine should you associate with Montagny?

options.text: Sweet Sémillon white from Sauternes
Dry Sauvignon Blanc from Centre-Loire
Dry Chardonnay white from the Côte Chalonnaise
Dry Gamay red from Beaujolais

mcqs.explanation: Montagny is associated with dry Chardonnay white wine in the Côte Chalonnaise, including Premier Cru sites. It commonly combines citrus or white-fruit flavours with freshness; oak and lees choices can change texture and aroma.

mcqs.prompt: Which distinction fits Alsace Vendanges Tardives and Sélection de Grains Nobles?

options.text: Neither term relates to fruit selection or harvest
VT uses late-harvest fruit; SGN selects suitably botrytised berries
Both terms require identical noble-rot selection in every wine
VT means a dry Pinot Noir red and SGN a sparkling white

mcqs.explanation: Alsace Vendanges Tardives uses late-harvest concentrated fruit; Sélection de Grains Nobles uses selective harvesting of suitably botrytised berries. Neither intense perfume nor the grape name alone establishes sweetness, and late harvest does not require noble rot in every VT wine.

mcqs.prompt: Which description fits Cabernet d’Anjou?

options.text: A Cabernet rosé with noticeable residual sweetness
A dry Cabernet Franc red from Chinon
A white Chenin sparkling wine
A Burgundy red made only from Gamay

mcqs.explanation: Cabernet d’Anjou is rosé with noticeable residual sweetness made from Cabernet Franc and Cabernet Sauvignon. Do not confuse the appellation with the dry Cabernet Franc reds of Chinon or Bourgueil.

mcqs.prompt: Which feature identifies Tavel among southern Rhône appellations?

options.text: It makes only dry Chardonnay whites
It is a sweet fortified Muscat appellation
It is a generic name for all southern French reds
It is rosé-only

mcqs.explanation: Tavel is a rosé-only appellation in the southern Rhône, using a Grenache-based blend. The name identifies protected origin and a rosé style, unlike Lirac, where red and white wines are also made.

mcqs.prompt: Which statement about Viognier in Côte-Rôtie reds is correct?

options.text: It must be present in every Côte-Rôtie
It is added only as sweet dosage after disgorgement
It can be included, but is optional
It must make up the entire wine

mcqs.explanation: Côte-Rôtie makes Syrah-based reds and can include Viognier, often co-fermented, to influence aroma and texture. Viognier is optional; a Côte-Rôtie does not have to contain it or follow one fixed blend percentage.

mcqs.prompt: Two Pays d’Oc whites are respectively steel-fermented Sauvignon Blanc and oak-influenced Chardonnay. What must a comparison consider?

options.text: The Sauvignon Blanc must be poorer because it uses steel
Different grapes and cellar choices as well as the shared origin
The origin requires identical aroma and texture
The Chardonnay must be sweeter because it is oaked

mcqs.explanation: A stainless-steel Sauvignon Blanc and an oak-influenced Chardonnay can differ markedly even when both carry Pays d’Oc IGP. Read variety and cuvée details and taste the wine before attributing differences solely to the shared region.

mcqs.prompt: What do Italian DOC and DOCG identify?

options.text: Protected-origin denominations with their own specifications
One universal grape and oak recipe
A finished-wine sweetness scale
Unregulated names for any wine made in Italy

mcqs.explanation: DOC and DOCG are traditional Italian terms for protected designation of origin wines. Each denomination has its own delimited origin and specification; the terms do not identify a universal grape or cellar recipe.

mcqs.prompt: What information does Classico primarily supply when permitted by an Italian appellation?

options.text: One identical barrel-ageing duration throughout Italy
The grape must be called Classico
A guarantee of stronger oak flavour
A defined traditional production area

mcqs.explanation: Classico refers to a defined traditional production area where the appellation’s rules permit the term. Chianti Classico is a separate appellation from Chianti. Classico does not identify an oak treatment, a grape variety or a universal ageing period.

mcqs.prompt: Why must a buyer check the specific appellation when interpreting Riserva?

options.text: Riserva is only a grape synonym
Riserva prohibits all bottle maturation
Additional requirements, including maturation, vary between appellations
Riserva means exactly the same ageing period everywhere

mcqs.explanation: Riserva signals additional requirements in an appellation’s specification, including maturation. Chianti Classico Riserva, for example, has a longer minimum maturation than Annata. Check the particular appellation; Riserva does not have one identical duration or oak programme across every Italian wine.

mcqs.prompt: Which grape is strongly associated with Delle Venezie DOC?

options.text: Cortese
Pinot Grigio
Fiano
Verdicchio

mcqs.explanation: Delle Venezie DOC is associated with Pinot Grigio from a production area spanning Veneto, Friuli Venezia Giulia and the Province of Trento. It is not identical to the Veneto administrative region or every wine made in northeastern Italy.

mcqs.prompt: Which distinction correctly links Cortese and Gavi?

options.text: Cortese is the grape; Gavi is the Piedmont wine origin
Gavi is a red grape and Cortese is the region
Both words describe dosage levels
Both are names for the same Tuscany town

mcqs.explanation: Gavi, also called Cortese di Gavi, is a Piedmont white-wine denomination associated with Cortese. Still dry examples commonly emphasise citrus or orchard fruit and freshness; Cortese is the grape, while Gavi is the origin.

mcqs.prompt: Both Amarone and Recioto della Valpolicella use dried grapes. Why does Recioto remain sweet?

options.text: Drying alone forces every resulting wine to be sweet
A second bottle fermentation removes the tannin
Sweetness is created by adding colour during riddling
Fermentation stops before all concentrated sugar is consumed

mcqs.explanation: Recioto della Valpolicella is a sweet red made from dried grapes. Drying concentrates the must, and fermentation is stopped before all the sugar is consumed; it is not made sweet simply because grapes have been dried.

mcqs.prompt: Which combination identifies Recioto di Soave?

options.text: Dry flor-aged fortified Palomino
White sparkling wine made only by force carbonation
Sweet white associated with Garganega and dried grapes
Dry red associated with Nebbiolo and fresh grapes

mcqs.explanation: Recioto di Soave is a sweet white wine associated with Garganega and appassimento. Grapes are dried before pressing to concentrate the must, and retained sugar differentiates it from the usual dry Soave study style.

mcqs.prompt: What does Montepulciano refer to in Vino Nobile di Montepulciano?

options.text: The method of second bottle fermentation
The Tuscan town and origin; the main association is Sangiovese
Proof that it uses the Montepulciano d’Abruzzo grape
A mandatory level of residual sugar

mcqs.explanation: Vino Nobile di Montepulciano is a Tuscan red associated with Sangiovese, locally called Prugnolo Gentile. Montepulciano here is the town and origin; Montepulciano d’Abruzzo is a different wine associated with the Montepulciano grape.

mcqs.prompt: Which grape family is associated with Frascati whites in Lazio?

options.text: Malvasia and Trebbiano
Nebbiolo and Dolcetto
Pinot Noir and Gamay
Tempranillo and Garnacha

mcqs.explanation: Frascati is a white-wine origin in Lazio, associated with Malvasia and Trebbiano. A Frascati Superiore producer example blends Malvasia di Candia, Malvasia del Lazio, Trebbiano Toscano and Grechetto. This example illustrates the regional white-grape family, not a universal blend recipe.

mcqs.prompt: Tinta de Toro is the local name for which central Toro red grape?

options.text: Mencía
Monastrell
Bobal
Tempranillo

mcqs.explanation: Toro red wines are strongly associated with Tinta de Toro, the local Tempranillo name, and the appellation also produces Garnacha-led reds. Both young fruit-led wines and wines matured in oak are made; Toro does not identify one compulsory oak flavour.

mcqs.prompt: Why can Garnacha make a pink Navarra wine rather than a deeply coloured red?

options.text: The appellation changes the berry colour after harvest
Rosé production excludes alcoholic fermentation
Shorter skin contact limits colour and tannin extraction
Pink wine requires white grapes only

mcqs.explanation: Navarra’s Garnacha rosés illustrate how a red grape can make a pink wine. Shorter skin contact limits colour and tannin extraction compared with a red wine; fruit ripeness, extraction and cellar choices still vary among producers.

mcqs.prompt: What do Rioja Crianza, Reserva and Gran Reserva communicate?

options.text: The same legal period for every red, white and rosé
Minimum maturation requirements that differ with wine colour
A compulsory single barrel origin for all wines
A guarantee of one identical aroma profile

mcqs.explanation: Rioja Crianza, Reserva and Gran Reserva specify minimum maturation requirements, with differences between reds and whites or rosés. Longer barrel and bottle maturation can alter tannin and aroma; the same label does not impose one barrel origin or a guaranteed taste.

mcqs.prompt: What prevents Catalunya DO from being treated as one red-grape recipe?

options.text: It includes white, rosé and red wines using several regional and international varieties
Every Catalunya wine is made only from Tempranillo
Only fortified reds qualify for the name
All permitted wines must have the same oak treatment

mcqs.explanation: Catalunya DO makes white, rosé and red wines from regional and international varieties. Tempranillo is an important study association, but Garnacha, Cariñena, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot and white varieties broaden the range.

mcqs.prompt: A German wine is labelled Spätlese. What extra information is needed before deciding its finished sweetness?

options.text: Only the grape skin colour
Only the bottle’s shape
Nothing: Spätlese always fixes one sweet palate
Residual sugar and fermentation outcome

mcqs.explanation: Prädikat terms principally describe grape maturity and harvest conditions under the applicable rules. Kabinett, Spätlese and Auslese can be made at different sweetness levels; fermentation and residual sugar must also be considered.

mcqs.prompt: Why can a Weinviertel DAC grape rule not be assumed for every Austrian DAC?

options.text: DAC removes all geographical requirements
Every DAC applies the same variety rules to all regions
Each DAC has its own prescribed regional grape and style profile
DAC is merely another word for all Grüner Veltliner

mcqs.explanation: DAC means Districtus Austriae Controllatus and identifies an Austrian regional quality-wine profile under a specific regulation. The required grapes and style differ by DAC; Weinviertel’s Grüner Veltliner rule does not apply automatically to Kamptal or Burgenland.

mcqs.prompt: Which set correctly links three Greek origins with important grape associations?

options.text: Naoussa–Carménère; Nemea–Malbec; Santorini–Sangiovese
Naoussa–Xinomavro; Nemea–Agiorgitiko; Santorini–Assyrtiko
Naoussa–Assyrtiko; Nemea–Xinomavro; Santorini–Agiorgitiko
Naoussa–Glera; Nemea–Furmint; Santorini–Cortese

mcqs.explanation: Naoussa is associated with Xinomavro reds, Nemea with Agiorgitiko reds and Santorini with Assyrtiko-led whites. Their grape structure and site or cellar practices must be explained separately rather than describe all Greek wine as one Mediterranean style.

mcqs.prompt: What acid change helps explain the common use of MLF in Chablis?

options.text: Malic acid becomes lactic acid, reducing acidity
Grape sugar becomes oak aroma
Lactic acid becomes tannin
MLF creates all the wine’s alcohol

mcqs.explanation: Most Chablis undergoes malolactic fermentation, converting malic to lactic acid and reducing acidity; the resulting balance remains wine-specific.

mcqs.prompt: A Douro wine is explicitly a still red. Which inference should be avoided?

options.text: That it can blend native varieties
That Touriga Nacional can be a component
That its blend can affect structure
That Douro origin means it was necessarily fortified like Port

mcqs.explanation: Douro still reds frequently blend native varieties such as Touriga Nacional, Touriga Franca and Tinta Roriz, with varietal examples also made. Blend composition helps explain structure and fruit expression; Port production methods must not be inferred from a Douro still-wine origin.

mcqs.prompt: Which qualification is correct when using Vinho Verde as a style guide?

options.text: Every bottle must be sweet red
All wines have identical carbonation and alcohol
Origin alone does not prove every wine is low-alcohol or lightly fizzy
Every bottle comes from unripe fruit

mcqs.explanation: Vinho Verde’s strong Atlantic influence, with substantial rainfall and moderate temperatures, supplies context for fresh aromatic whites from grapes including Alvarinho and Loureiro. The name does not establish that every wine is low in alcohol, lightly fizzy or made from unripe fruit.

mcqs.prompt: Which grape is strongly associated with structured Dão white wines?

options.text: Monastrell
Encruzado
Glera
Gamay

mcqs.explanation: Encruzado is strongly associated with Dão and can combine acidity with a structured white-wine palate in varietal wines or blends. This supports comparison with lighter aromatic whites, while harvest and cellar choices prevent a fixed richness or ageing rule.

mcqs.prompt: Why are exposure and site energy relevant to a Mosel Riesling comparison?

options.text: Riesling ripens slowly and retains marked acidity
Riesling must always be sweet regardless of site
Acidity proves every vineyard has the same temperature
The regional label removes the need to assess maturity

mcqs.explanation: Riesling ripens slowly and retains marked acidity, so suitable exposure and site energy matter. Its Mosel association does not fix sweetness: Riesling has dry and sweet expressions, and the actual wine needs checking.
